cohort: The study included 21 patients with neonatal AIS and 7 patients with presumed neonatal AIS identified in Aichi Prefecture, Japan, between 2010 and 2014.
finding: The study found differences in clinical-radiological features, sequelae, and emergency cesarean section rates between neonatal AIS and presumed neonatal AIS, suggesting different causal factors and potentially undiagnosed cases of presumed neonatal AIS.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean sections were more common in neonatal AIS (43%) than in presumed neonatal AIS (13%), suggesting different causal factors related to mode of birth for the two conditions.
